analysis.title: Blue-nami Hangover: Chips Bounce, Breadth Doesn't As Hot Payrolls Put December Hike Back On The Table
key_insights: Friday Nov 6 was a morning-after bounce following Thursday's sharp selloff. Dip-buying and short-covering in the most-beaten AI/semis names lifted the Nasdaq, but most S&P stocks closed lower.

Payrolls rose 165K vs a 70K median estimate, with unemployment down to 4.1%. This weakened the growth-scare narrative and revived a December rate hike, bear-flattening the curve, lifting the dollar and pressuring gold and bitcoin.
The week's damage: Nasdaq's worst day since Covid, a record put-volume day, a record split in levered vs inverse ETF flows, and S&P down about 2%.

The bounce was narrow. Only 44% of SPX names advanced, cap-weight beat equal-weight by nearly 80bps, and the median S&P stock fell 0.24%. StoneX and Goldman's TMT desk described it as short covering and bargain hunting with a lack of conviction.

Goldman's prime brokerage data shows Global Fundamental L/S managers down 1.3% on the week (a -2 SD move), and TMT L/S funds down more than 4%, now roughly flat YTD from about +24% before the June/July AI sell-off.

Goldman's Vol Panic Index hit 9.57 out of 10, VVIX posted its 2nd largest one-day rise ever, and over 11 million puts traded on Thursday, a record. Goldman traders said extreme panic readings have historically preceded strong medium-term rebounds, but not necessarily a reason to rush back into risk.

Discretionary hedge funds were not the main sellers. US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% in a day and net leverage fell to 71.8% (4th percentile on a 1-year basis) while gross stayed at 314% (97th percentile on 5 years). Retail and levered-ETF flows drove the action.

ETFs printed $580BN of notional volume Thursday (33% of the tape), QQQ set a notional record at $86BN, and levered semis printed over $37BN. Levered ETFs also took in record inflows on the same day, meaning dip buyers used 3x leverage.

SPX liquidity is thin, with top-of-book depth about $4MM Thursday and $3MM Friday. Goldman estimates CTAs have about $28BN of SPX to sell over the next week in a flat tape, with SPX below the 7,547 medium-term threshold. The European desk warned negative dealer gamma leaves scope for violent moves either way.

Asia's AI supply chain was hit harder: KOSPI fell 12% on the week, MSCI EM fell 4%, and Taiwan saw its second-largest weekly foreign selling on record. Taiwan curbed short-selling and readied a $15BN fund, and Seoul waived margin calls. India's NIFTY rose 9% and China gained 2-5% on the week.

Rates: the front end sold off about 5bps and the curve bear-flattened, with 2s10s at 33bps and the 10Y up 2bps to 4.85%. Money markets priced about 20bps of a December hike. Goldman's rates strategists said the print reinforces the Fed's focus on inflation, and that Tuesday's CPI is the decisive data point.

Credit barely moved. On Thursday, with the S&P down 4.4%, generic IG spreads widened 3.6bps vs 8.2bps implied by regression (Goldman Credit MarketStrats). Hyperscalers are on pace to fund 36% of capex with credit this year, only 43% of $687BN of AI-linked financing came from hyperscalers, and state moratoriums could affect about 45% of planned US data center capacity.
Dollar index up 0.4%, EUR fell 0.7% to 1.1141, USDJPY at 158.49. Gold fell 0.6% to about $4,063. Bitcoin was flat near $75.6K, with a $6.3BN Binance hack weighing on sentiment.

Oil whipsawed on Hormuz mine headlines and US-Iran deal headlines. Brent ranged $97-101 and settled at $98.32, WTI settled at $90.83. Brent is down from about $115 last week to about $97, and hedge funds cut net bullish Brent bets to a 3-month low.

Goldman launched a 'Hormuz Transit' basket to play a peace deal. Names in it rallied 30% since the war began, now trade 25% rich to their 5-year history, and consensus sees 75% of the basket with declining earnings in 2027/28.

Microsoft is winding down its deal to rent AI cloud capacity from Oracle as part of a wider reassessment of cloud partnerships. Bloomberg reported Anthropic IPO buyers now see valuations as low as $1.1 trillion. Baseload power names (Power-Up America basket) caught a bid.

Author's view: Friday was probably a dead-cat bounce rather than the bottom. The tell is credit, since IG catching down to equities would mean Thursday was not the low. The long-term Nasdaq support is the big test.
Next week: CPI Tuesday, PPI Friday, earnings from NRG and AMAT, Russia/Ukraine/US talks in Abu Dhabi Nov 10-11. Nvidia reports at the end of the month.

tension_points.bull_case: Panic gauges are at extremes, put buying is at records, net leverage is near lows and SOX multiples are back near 2022 levels, with NVDA at 10x blended 24-month forward. Goldman traders say extreme panic historically precedes strong medium-term rebounds.
tension_points.bear_case: The bounce was narrow, with 44% of SPX names advancing and the median stock down. CTAs have about $28BN to sell, credit has not repriced, dip buying came via 3x levered ETFs, and the Fed may keep hiking into an AI capex slowdown.
tension_points.what_invalidates: IG credit catching down to equities, or another sizable drawdown breaking the long-term Nasdaq support.
